notes: Cross-vendor judge (MiniMax M3) on an isolated clone of the executor's head; the executor's claims were treated as claims until reproduced. Reproduced green: AC1, AC2, AC2a, AC2b, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC6a, AC7 and 5 of AC8's 6 gates, plus every byte-exact sha256 the plan names (test d77c1dc9, record 43f2f7e2, runner 6a950825, manifest ff14f59f, layout 0b433ca7) and the MS1 RED (52/4). Nine mutants of my own: six killed the gate, one (M9) killed the pin for an undrilled check, one (M8) proved the runner reads the pin live and fails closed, and two guard-bypass mutants (M5 the loose pin, M6 the broken restore check) SURVIVED - which is the evidence that the count pin and the fail-closed restore are load-bearing. No blocking finding. The row's substance (D-148 A: Voyage and Crew 0.275 m back, 1.50 m from the desk, in the manifest and the deck layout, with the pins re-computed) is implemented exactly and independently verified. The runner writes only inside the clone and its own mktemp dir, and every exit path (timeout, INT, TERM, dirty tree, restore fault) leaves the tree clean. Recommendation: land after amending the design doc's V28/AC10 to the measured 52/4 and adding the controller ruling to the ledger; AC11 (Mark's look) stays a separate attended step.
